    *   Use the message: 'MUI Grid2: The `zeroMinWidth` prop has been removed and is no longer necessary. You can safely remove it.'
    *   Ensure this warning is emitted only once per session.
*   Emit a console warning for any theme breakpoint prop (e.g., xs, sm, md, lg, xl) passed to the Grid2 component.
    *   Use the message pattern: 'MUI Grid2: The `{breakpoint}` prop has been removed. See https://mui.com/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/ for migration instructions.'

*   Update the `replaceMaterialLinks` utility to handle URL transformations.
    *   Map the path `/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/` to `/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/`.
    *   Ensure the old path `/migration/migration-grid-v2/` is no longer used.

The verification system will apply test patches automatically.

Here's what I found about the MUI Grid2 `"The item prop has been removed and is no longer necessary"` warning.

## What the warning means

This console warning appears when you're using the modern MUI Grid (Grid v2) but still passing the legacy `item` prop from Grid v1. In the updated Grid, this prop was intentionally removed. All grids are considered items without specifying the item prop. In other words, one of the key differences between Grid v1 and v2 is that in v2, you don't need to specify the item prop for grid items. In v2, every direct child of a Grid container is automatically treated as a grid item.

## How to fix it

Simply remove the `item` (and `zeroMinWidth`) props from your Grid components. The item and zeroMinWidth props have been removed in the updated Grid. You can safely remove them: `-<Grid item zeroMinWidth>` becomes `+<Grid>`.

## Background on the warning behavior

The specific warning text you mentioned relates to work the MUI team did to improve the migration experience. There was originally a known gap in developer feedback here. According to the Grid2 rollout plan discussion, there was no clear warning when doing `<Grid2 item>`, and the team concluded they needed a custom prop type instead, that clearly explains that this is a Grid v1 prop that you can now remove.

Regarding the `createGrid` / `deleteLegacyGridProps` internals you referenced: these are part of the Grid's internal implementation that strips out (deletes) the deprecated legacy props like `item`, `zeroMinWidth`, and the breakpoint props (`xs`, `sm`, etc.) when they're passed to the newer Grid, and emits the console warning telling you they're no longer necessary. The search results don't contain the specific source code for `createGrid` and `deleteLegacyGridProps`, so I can't detail their exact implementation.

## Also worth noting for the migration

If you're on a newer version, the breakpoint props have also changed. The Grid component has been stabilized in Material UI v6, so the unstable prefix is removed — you can import via `import Grid from '@mui/material/Grid2'` or `import { Grid2 } from '@mui/material'`. The size and offset properties for corresponding breakpoints have also been renamed. This means, along with removing `item`, you should convert props like `xs={6}` to the new `size` syntax, e.g. `<Grid size={{ xs: 12, sm: 6 }}>`.

The good news is MUI provides codemods to automate most of this. You can run the official MUI codemods to fix common breaking changes automatically — though note the codemods won't cover styled or wrapped Grid components, which you'll need to update manually.

For the complete official migration steps, see MUI's "Upgrade to Grid v2" guide at mui.com/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/.
